title: fnox: make it the standard way agents and operators get secrets
description: fnox (deepwatrcreatur/fnox-flake, jdx/fnox 1.19) is installed on every Linux HM host with an age store, seed sources and wrappers (gh-fnox, bw-fnox, claude-code-fnox, attic-fnox, pbs), but it is underused. On 2026-11-22 the agent working the router PRs ran 'export GH_TOKEN=$(cat ~/.config/git/github-token)' and an inline credential helper that cats the token for every gh and git push call, instead of fnox. This epic covers the guideline change, fixing what blocks fnox use today, and a survey for further agent and homelab uses. Acceptance: children closed; agents' default secret path is fnox (exec, wrappers, git helper), documented in nix-agent-guides and synced into every repo.

title: Agent guidelines: use fnox for secrets; never export or cat token files
description: Update nix-agent-guides (CONVENTIONS.md and the synced agents-core block, then run scripts/sync-agents-core.sh so every Nix repo gets it) and unified agent-guides/tooling.md. Rules: (1) run commands needing a secret through a fnox wrapper (gh is aliased to gh-fnox; note aliases do not apply in non-interactive agent shells, so call gh-fnox or 'fnox exec -- <cmd>' explicitly); (2) never 'export X=$(cat <secret file>)' or 'X=$(fnox get ...)' into a long-lived shell; scope to one command with 'fnox exec -- cmd'; (3) git push over HTTPS uses the fnox git credential helper (sibling bead), not an inline helper that cats a file; (4) never print secret values; compare by hash when debugging; (5) how to add a new secret (fnox set / seedSecretSources) and where agenix still applies (system services). Include copy-paste examples for gh, git push, curl with a bearer token, and nix with an access-tokens header. Acceptance: block merged in nix-agent-guides, synced to unified, nix-clan-homelab, nix-router-optimized; the memory/agent docs that showed the old pattern are corrected.
close_reason: Done 2026-11-27. nix-agent-guides #10 + #11: guides/secrets.md (fnox for command secrets, clan vars/agenix for services; rules; examples for gh, git push, curl, nix; probing a secret without the ambient token), CONVENTIONS + shared block v4. Synced: unified #267, nix-clan-homelab #83, nix-router-optimized #194, fnox-flake #27 (also fixed its argv seeding and fnox-get verify steps), nix-attic-infra #15 (also fixed debug commands that printed the attic token). git credential helper remains nch-a67.3; on emerald fnox exec still yields 'age' until the fnox-flake #26 rollout (nch-a67.2).

title: fnox is non-functional on emerald: no age identity, 'default = age' rendering, seeding never runs
description: Found 2026-11-22: 'fnox get GITHUB_TOKEN' returns a token GitHub rejects (HTTP 401), while ~/.config/git/github-token (its first seed source) works; gh-fnox still works, apparently via the seed file. So agents that call fnox directly get a dead credential, which pushes them back to reading files. Fix the immediate drift (reseed from the source of truth), then make drift detectable: decide whether seed sources or the age store are authoritative per secret, make the seed script refresh changed sources, and add a 'fnox-check' style command or HM activation check that validates freshness (hash compare against the seed source, never printing values; optional live probe such as 'gh api user' for GITHUB_TOKEN). Acceptance: fnox get GITHUB_TOKEN works on emerald; a check reports drift for any seeded secret; documented in fnox-flake.
notes:
Root cause (2026-11-22, emerald), worse than drift:
1. NO AGE IDENTITY. fnox encrypts to the two legacy SOPS age recipients from unified .sops.yaml (age17mn5ln..., age1awqed0...). FNOX_AGE_KEY_FILE points at ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt, which does not exist on emerald, so nothing in the store decrypts (identity_read_failed). Neither recipient matches emerald's user or host SSH key.
2. fnox-flake lib mkFnoxConfigToml renders each declared secret as 'default = <provider>'. In fnox, 'default' is the fallback VALUE, so every unseeded secret (GITHUB_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ATTIC_CLIENT_JWT_TOKEN, BW_SESSION, GEMINI, GROK, OPENCODE_ZEN, OPENROUTER, PROXMOX_API_TOKEN, Z_AI) resolves to the literal string 'age' (the HTTP 401). Fix: render 'provider = <provider>' so unseeded secrets are reported missing.
3. unified's seed script (modules/home-manager/common/fnox.nix) skips any secret that 'fnox get' returns, so (2) blocks seeding forever; it also passes values on argv (visible in ps). Fix drafted on unified branch fix/fnox-reseed-on-drift (reseed when the stored value differs; value on stdin), untestable until (1) is solved.
4. gh-fnox looked healthy because gh falls back to its own stored login when GH_TOKEN is empty; this also fooled the agent's first verification.
Operator decision needed for (1): provision the SOPS age key to emerald and every fnox host, or move fnox to per-host identities (age recipients from each host's user SSH key via ssh-to-age, or ssh-ed25519 recipients if fnox's age provider accepts them) and re-encrypt.

description: fnox looks underused. title: elitedesk X520 LAN port dropped off PCIe
description: At 2026-11-18 17:13:33 EST, ~2.5 h after boot, the kernel logged 'ixgbe 0000:01:00.1: Adapter removed' and 'firmware error detected FWSM: 0xFFFFFFFF'; enp1s0f1 (LAN, DAC) lost carrier. No AER or thermal messages. Driver rebind and PCI FLR both failed (probe error -5); a warm reboot restored the port at 10 Gb/s. A router whose LAN NIC can vanish is not fit to be primary. Investigate: card temperature and airflow (X520s run hot in small chassis), PCIe ASPM (try pcie_aspm=off), slot seating, firmware; add a Prometheus alert for ixgbe 'Adapter removed' and link loss; watch for recurrence over a multi-day soak. Acceptance: root cause or mitigation applied, plus 7 days without recurrence before elitedesk becomes primary.

title: elitedesk X520 loses TCP replies (Flow Director ATR suspected)
description:
Found 2026-11-19 in the zoneReplication.ha rehearsal. Symptom: ~3.6% of TCP DNS queries from elitedesk to router 10.10.10.1:53 time out (18/504 over 10 min); UDP 0/504; emerald 0/1170 over TCP+UDP in the same window. Packet capture on elitedesk: router never answers the SYN (neither the ECN SYN nor the plain retry); 13/14 other ECN SYNs were answered, so ECN is not the cause, and the source port was not reused. Router-side listen overflows were disproven as the cause (round 1): they belong to router-dashboard :8888 (nch-sny.35). Impact: zone transfers (TCP), DoT/large answers, and the HA SOA check (now retried 3x, nix-router-optimized#149) -- a real failover risk.

Test plan (each round recorded here):
1. Attribute: which process/listener overflows (ss -ltn Recv-Q sampling, nstat deltas per minute), which clients open TCP :53 most (conntrack by src), and whether bursts line up with Technitium tasks (blocklist update, zone transfer, stats).
2. Reproduce on demand: parallel TCP query load from a LAN host; compare elitedesk vs emerald vs a third host; vary ECN on/off.
3. Fix candidates: raise the listen backlog (net.core.somaxconn and Technitium's TCP backlog/accept settings), tune Technitium TCP options, check router CPU/thread starvation; one change at a time.
4. Verify: overnight probe from >=2 hosts over TCP and UDP plus AXFR, zero timeouts; overflows on the :53 listener zero (bpftrace per-port; the host-wide counter includes router-dashboard :8888, tracked in nch-sny.35); repeat on elitedesk as the DNS server before any failover.
Acceptance: root cause named, fix deployed, round 4 clean on both routers.

Pass/fail gate (discussion 21): before VRRP is enabled or elitedesk is promoted, a 24 h probe from elitedesk to router and from another LAN host to elitedesk (TCP and UDP, 1 query/s each, plus hourly AXFR) must show zero TCP reply losses, no ixgbe 'Adapter removed', no AER errors and no unexpected carrier changes. Any recurrence means swapping the X520 for the ConnectX-4 Lx and re-running the gate.
close_reason: Resolved by replacing the X520 with a ConnectX-4 Lx; 24 h gate passed both directions with 0 TCP/UDP failures (see comment).

comments.author: deepwatrcreatur
comments.text:
Round 1 (2026-11-19, attribution), corrects the hypothesis in the description:
- Router's ListenOverflows come from router-dashboard :8888 (backlog 5), shown with a bpftrace kprobe on tcp_conn_request; :53 never filled. That's a separate small bug.
- Simultaneous captures on router (any iface) and elitedesk (-i any): for every failed connection router received the SYN and sent SYN-ACK out enp6s16, retransmitting 6+ times over 16 s. elitedesk received none of them on any interface. Other connections in the same seconds worked.
- Not deterministic per 4-tuple: reusing the failed source ports later always succeeded. UDP never fails, and emerald never fails.
- Suspect: X520/82599 Flow Director ATR (hashes TCP flows; UDP RSS ignores ports). This driver has no flow-director-atr priv flag; ntuple on disables ATR.
- A/B so far is inconclusive: ATR off gave 0/400 and 0/400, but the ATR-on control also gave 0/400; earlier ATR-on runs failed 1-8%. Toggling ntuple may flush a stale fdir table.
- Running: 2 h TCP+UDP soak on elitedesk with ntuple on (unit dns-soak-atr-off, runtime-only setting).
Next rounds: (2) 2 h soak with ATR on as control; (3) a third LAN host and switch-port/cable check, ruling out the switch; (4) if ATR is confirmed, persist ntuple on (or a module option) and verify overnight on both TCP and UDP plus AXFR.

comments.author: deepwatrcreatur
comments.text: E15 (12 h ATR-on control) is void for ATR: from 22:13 the whole X520 dropped off PCIe (nch-sny.31 recurrence), so every query failed. Before 22:13 the only failures were the known 21:30-21:35 outage window (10 TCP, 10 UDP, both protocols, so not ATR). If the X520 is replaced by the ConnectX-4 Lx, the ATR question becomes moot; re-run the 24 h gate on the new NIC.

title: Delegated-prefix unreachable route lost when router-ha-ra-owner restarts on a MASTER
description: 2026-11-26 19:30: deploying #193 restarted router-ha-ra-owner on elitedesk (MASTER, WAN up). Its two LAN reconfigures (networkctl reload with the drop-in removed, then re-added) left the WAN's 'unreachable <PD>/56 proto dhcp' route missing; networkctl reconfigure of the WAN restored it. comments.author: codex
comments.text: NixCI's cache docs (https://nix-ci.com/documentation/nix-ci-cache) describe user-token access as ReadAllowed for repositories accessible to that account and WriteAllowed only for that user's private namespace; they do not document a read-only token scope. The proposed router path uses a separate Clan var generator (nix-ci-cache-auth/netrc) on elitedesk/router only, and the config check rejects Attic-token or remote-builder generators on either router. This is NixCI-only but not read-only: the token retains its account repository-read scope and can write to its private namespace. A dedicated account with narrower repository access is the documented boundary if narrower read access is required.

NixCI token access cannot guarantee that a given package path exists in its cache. title: Roll out router hardening (PR #61) to router and elitedesk
description: Upstream work tracked as nix-router-optimized router-mwb (discussion 23). UPDATE 2026-11-25: nix-router-optimized already ships services.router-security-hardened (kernelHardening: kptr/dmesg restrict, unprivileged BPF off, fs.protected_*, no redirects/source routes, protocol blacklist); router-role does not enable it, probably because it mkForces rp_filter=1 while router-role sets loose rp_filter=2. Per decision 0003: first an upstream PR making rp_filter configurable, using install-false instead of blacklist only, adding bpf_jit_harden and suid_dumpable; then rework #61 to enable the upstream module in router-role. Original plan follows. PR #61 adds modules/aspects/router-hardening.nix (self-includes into router-role): network sysctls (rp_filter, no redirects/source routes, syncookies, martian logging), kernel sysctls (kptr_restrict, dmesg_restrict, unprivileged BPF off, ptrace scope), uncommon protocol modules blacklisted via install <proto> coreutils false, SSH KbdInteractiveAuthentication off, documentation.nixos off. Rationale and deliberate omissions (sysrq kept for console recovery, no forwarding changes) in docs/router-hardening.md. Held until the VRRP drill (nch-sny.36) ends because elitedesk is the live primary. Steps: merge #61; deploy the backup node first, check sysctl values, routing/NAT, VRRP adverts and SSH; then the primary in a maintenance window with console access. Acceptance: both nodes run it, docs record the result.
close_reason: clan #61 (e412c13) merged and deployed to router and elitedesk 2026-11-28: router-security-hardened kernelHardening with loose rp_filter; sshd restarted, sysctls applied, no failed units.

title: Extend SSH and kernel hardening beyond the routers
description: From the RGBCube/ncc review (2026-11-25). #61 applies hardening only to router-role. Before writing more local hardening, compare with srvos (nix-community, used by clan users; server mixin sets many of the same SSH and sysctl options) and the nixpkgs hardened profile; prefer importing srvos mixins and overriding where they conflict. Then decide what suits servers, Proxmox guests and workstations: KbdInteractiveAuthentication off (advertised though PAM denies it), kptr/dmesg restrict, unprivileged BPF off, protocol blacklist. Exclude what breaks workstations (ptrace scope breaks debuggers) or console recovery. Consider moving router-hardening's generic parts upstream into nix-router-optimized. Revisit a capability-based systemd sandbox base when LXC services migrate. Acceptance: decision recorded, aspect or srvos import merged with a check, applied to one non-router host.

title: router: drop un-NATed LAN hairpin while a new MASTER's WAN comes up
description: 2026-11-27: phoenix's WireGuard (UDP, keepalive) died at the 20:38 fail-back. On the new MASTER the LAN fallback route (via the VIP, metric 2000) is the only default until the WAN's DHCP route arrives; a forwarded client packet leaves the LAN un-NATed and its conntrack entry has no NAT; a flow that keeps sending never lets it expire, so its packets left the WAN with a private source forever. Fixed live by deleting the entry. Acceptance: forward rule dropping lan->lan to non-LAN destinations, check, deployed to both.

title: realvnc-vnc-viewer 7.15.1 source URL is gone (404); fresh workstation builds fail
description:
nixpkgs' realvnc-vnc-viewer 7.15.1 (both unified's 2026-08-12 and this repo's 2026-11-16 pin) downloads https://downloads.realvnc.com/download/file/viewer.files/VNC-Viewer-7.15.1-Linux-x64.rpm, which now returns 404. It is unfree, so cache.nixos.org has no copy. modules/_nixos/workstation.nix installs it (unified: profiles/nixos/workstation.nix), so any host without the built path fails to build: found 2026-11-22 rebuilding phoenix from unified main. workstation-niri-eval only evaluates drvPaths, so checks don't catch it.
Stopgap (2026-11-22): the built path /nix/store/y6hpf2kzpk1nh4005wvkd3saw83vzqi9-realvnc-vnc-viewer-7.15.1 was copied from phoenix and pushed to attic cache-local, which clan and unified hosts use as a substituter. It stays valid only while the nixpkgs pin produces that exact path.
Fix: override src to a RealVNC release that still downloads (check RealVNC's download page for the current version and hash), or drop the package if nothing uses it. Add a build check like checks.omasnap so a dead source fails CI.
Acceptance: nix build of the workstation's realvnc-vnc-viewer succeeds with attic cache-local disabled (--option substituters https://cache.nixos.org); a flake check builds it.
close_reason: Removed realvnc-vnc-viewer from the workstation package set (operator doesn't use it; upstream download gone): this PR, plus unified-nix-configuration profiles/nixos/workstation.nix. remmina stays for VNC. The attic cache-local copy is no longer needed.
